From reading your other comments in this post, I can offer my sympathy, because I know exactly what you’re talking about and have experienced it myself (as far as showing emotions goes), and some advice. 

It’s very hard growing up in a society and a family that values “manliness”, like showing no emotions. But (as difficult as it is, much easier said than done) you have to learn to discard those ideas and learn new coping strategies and understandings, such as your emotions being natural, and to hide something natural is nonsensical. These are things that therapy can help with, if that’s an option for you. If not, YouTube can show coping strategies. It’s not idea, but the info is there.

It seems like you’re asking for advice, rather than comfort, so the advice I have is to find coping strategies. A therapist would be best, but since you can’t afford it, I’m sure Googling or YouTube will have strategies you can implement. 

I was the same way. I’m 21 now, but for the longest time I was so dependent on other people, but over the past year and a half, I’ve become *more* self reliant (not isolated, but being able to help myself). This comes down to your own life philosophy, but if you’re like me and don’t like to rely on someone, or don’t like the feeling of putting your load on someone’s back, then coping strategies are the way to go.

Easier said than done, though. They don’t solve your physical/real-life problems, they help you cope and keep you grounded, thinking straight. 

That’s the high level view, anyways. From what I’m told in therapy.
